chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Ali ibn al-Hakam, all from Abu Yahya al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the voluntary prayer (nafl) during the day while traveling, and he said, 'O my son, if the voluntary prayer were valid/perfect during travel, the obligatory prayer would be completed (i.e., reduced to two rak'ahs as nafl is).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for voluntary prayers during the day while traveling in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential link between voluntary and obligatory prayers during travel by using a conditional analogy: if the *nafl* prayer were deemed sufficient or complete in its own right while traveling, it would logically entail that the obligatory *fard* prayer is also fulfilled or reduced. This highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that *nafl* acts as a supplementary act of worship that does not replace the core obligation, reinforcing the structural integrity of the five daily prayers even in states of travel or shortening (*qasr*).
